Figure 32 shows how the stats data is stored within the UserStats model class. 
The key aspects to note are that all stat types inherit from Stats, ensuring that 
each has Bronze, Silver and Gold ranking boundaries, a current rank, and a 
boolean to determine weather the user has progressed rank since last viewing 
the stat. The exact implementation of each stat type varies; however, they will 
typically have a counter to gauge how far the user has progressed. All stat types 
are finally stored and managed within the UserStats Class. 
 
Figure 33 Display Achievements Front-end Sequence Diagram 
Considering Figure 32, the stats handler converts the JSON string returned in 
the response body into the UserStats model, via its constructor. Once the 
UserStats object has been initialised, the ViewModel can then display data by 
repeating the respective Views, for each stat type. It is also worth noting the 
reset rank changed, and that it marks the entry as viewed, this API will be later 
defined in Table 24.
